evidence: app/react-router.config.ts:3 — only sets ssr: true, the framework-mode default; no future flags, no experimental config
app/app/root.tsx:1-11 — only long-stable RR exports (Link, Links, Meta, Outlet, Scripts, ScrollRestoration, isRouteErrorResponse)
app/app/routes.ts:1-10 — stable index/route config helpers, no unstable_ imports anywhere in app source
app/app/routes/move.tsx:22 — standard loader/meta route-module exports, stable since v7 and default in v8
app/package.json:4-12 — react-router ^8.5.1 and vite ^8.0.3, both current stable releases (RR 8.5.0 published Oct 2026, vite 8.0.0 stable 2026-03-12)
reach.rationale: The app relies exclusively on APIs that have been stable for one or more majors; it touches none of the unstable v8.4/8.5 features (API-only mode, route-discovery control, custom fetch metadata) and uses current stable dependency versions.

evidence: app/app/lib/data.server.ts:5-36 — data access is a self-contained plain-fetch module; no experimental data-layer APIs to leak out
app/vite.config.ts:1-9 — minimal plugin config; the only lockfile reference to @vitejs/plugin-rsc (package-lock.json:384) is transitive, not app code
containment.rationale: There is nothing experimental to contain; the few borderline-new things (vite 8's Rolldown, React 19) are locked behind ordinary dependency versions rather than feature flags.

evidence: app/app/root.tsx:33-49 — hash scrolling hand-rolled with useEffect/useLocation instead of reaching for newer framework conveniences
app/app/routes/home.tsx:123-130 — pagination/search via stable useSearchParams/useState rather than experimental router features
justification.rationale: No experimental or preview APIs are used at all, so there is no unjustified reach; where the framework offers newer options (view transitions, RSC, middleware) the app sensibly sticks with stable ones, which is the right call since view transitions are being deprecated in 8.5.0.

findings.issue: ssr: true is the framework-mode default, so the config flag is redundant (harmless, but slightly misleading as to whether non-default behavior is intended)
findings.suggestion: Either drop the config file or add a comment noting SSR is the default and the flag is kept for explicitness

summary: The app has zero exposure to experimental, preview, RC, or canary APIs: it pins the current stable React Router 8.5.x and Vite 8, sets no experimental or future flags, and uses only loader/meta/route-component APIs that have been stable since v6/v7. This is the low-risk posture you want for an app a team will own for years. The only adjacent nit is a redundant ssr: true flag in the config.
